notes: Also selects the risk-free tenor: the 7y point for a 7-year projection.

debt_spread.source: assumption carried over from the first DCF version, where it was hardcoded; pre-tax spread over the risk-free rate, no rating-based source wired yet

bank_nii_ratio_threshold.source: assumption: net interest income as a share of total revenue at or above which a company is a bank. A sign test is not usable because the vendor reports a net interest income row for every company. 0.25 missed ITUB (0.215), whose fee and insurance income dilutes the ratio; 0.15 still sits about 150x above MSFT (0.001). Ratios on yfinance 1.7.0, 2026-09-18: JPM 0.525, GS 0.233, ITUB 0.215, MS 0.152, MSFT 0.001

growth_clamp_lower.source: growth clamp from the original parameter file (growth_clamp.lower); bounds the derived starting growth, and binding is recorded

growth_clamp_upper.source: growth clamp from the original parameter file (growth_clamp.upper); bounds the derived starting growth, and binding is recorded

mean_reversion_lambda.source: mean reversion from the original parameter file (mean_reversion.lambda, enabled)
notes: Mean reversion causes growth rates to decay toward terminal growth. lambda controls speed: 0.1=slow (reaches terminal ~year 10), 0.25=moderate (~year 4), 0.5=fast (~year 2). Set enabled=false for constant growth (legacy behavior).

mature_market_erp.source: Damodaran, mature-market equity risk premium, January 2026 vintage (the base of the total-ERP table); a domicile's country risk premium is its total ERP less this

midcycle_window_years.source: long enough to hold two oil cycles (the 2014-16 downturn, 2020, the 2022 spike); a shorter window measures one phase
notes: The mid-cycle DCF's window: every annual period the record carries, newest first, up to this many; the fetch keeps this many periods for a class whose first admissible model is dcf_midcycle, five for every other model.

The reinvestment floor (33): a reinvestment rate of about -0.10 over ten to fifteen years is capital roughly maintained, with depreciation and working-capital release slightly ahead of capex, not a business selling itself off; a guard cannot tell the two apart and any threshold that could would be a tuned parameter. A negative measured rate is therefore read as no net reinvestment through the cycle: mid-cycle free cash flow equals mid-cycle profit and growth from reinvestment is zero. It drops the disinvestment cash entirely, conservative in the one direction that matters, and the reversion from zero starting growth to the terminal rate is the simplification every DCF path already makes for a name whose capex equals its depreciation. The measured rate stays on the record beside the floored one.

midcycle_scale_floor.source: a year in which the business was under a tenth of its present capital is a different business; two commodity cycles fit inside a tenfold range, a hundredfold does not
notes: The mid-cycle return average takes NOPAT_t over the prior period's invested capital. A period whose opening invested capital is below this fraction of the latest period's is left out of that average and listed on the record as an exclusion reading "opening capital below the scale floor"; the eight-observation guard then counts what remains, so a name with too little comparable history fails with the count rather than valuing on a ratio about a smaller company.

The reinvestment rate is untouched: it is a ratio of sums over the window, and a year whose flows were a hundredth of today's barely enters either sum, so the distortion the floor corrects does not arise there.
Changing the floor is a dated declaration, not a tuning knob: the value was set once, from the shape of the window (fifteen years, meant to hold two commodity cycles), not from any name's output.

interest_evidence_floor.source: half a percent of operating income is the scale of an undrawn facility's fees, not of borrowing
notes: The debt definition's absent-is-zero rule (25) asks the filing to say twice that a filer owes nothing: no debt line and no interest. (65) A trace of interest is not that second saying. Deckers files no borrowing of any kind and tags interest of two tenths of a per cent of operating income, the fees on an undrawn facility; Williams-Sonoma files none and tags five hundredths of a per cent beside net interest income of far more. Below this fraction the interest is not evidence of debt and the rule fires; at or above it the field stays null, as before.

The floor is applied only where operating income is filed and positive: a filer with no operating income line, or a loss, has no scale to measure the interest against, so the evidence stands and the field stays null. That is what leaves Ford, whose latest operating income is negative, exactly where it was.
Interest that is income is never evidence of debt whatever its size, which is the sign half of the same rule and needs no parameter.

sensitivity_steps.source: readability steps, not standard deviations: one fixed symmetric step per input kind, chosen so a reader can compare names on the same move; nothing here is estimated from history or a prior, and a step changes by a decision, never after seeing a result
notes: growth: starting growth or ROE0, plus or minus 2 percentage points. lambda: plus or minus 0.10. terminal_growth: plus or minus 0.5 percentage points. discount_rate: WACC or the cost of equity, plus or minus 1 percentage point. base_fraction: the cash-flow base (FCFF, FCFF_mid, the covered dividend per share, book equity), plus or minus 10 percent.

frontier_draws.source: the frontier's sample size (35): enough that the declared correlation reproduces within a hundredth and the 5% tail holds a thousand draws; fixed so two runs agree, and a change is a decision

frontier_seed.source: the sampler's seed (35): fixed so two runs are byte-identical; a change is a decision, never a way to a nicer number

terminal_growth_rate.source: IMF World Economic Outlook, April 2026 vintage: gross domestic product, current prices, national currency (series NGDP, unit XDC, current prices), percent change at the last year of the projection horizon, 2031; transcribed by hand
notes: The method: the terminal cash flow is in the country's own currency, so the anchor is long-run nominal growth in that currency. The WEO's last projected year is the nearest thing to a long run that anyone publishes on the record, and it is deliberately not the current year, which carries the cycle. The figure is the percent change of the nominal level between the final two projected years, 2030 to 2031.

Vintage: the World Economic Outlook is published each April and October. This is the April 2026 edition, released on 14 April 2026, established from the data itself -- the projection horizon ends in 2031, which no earlier vintage reaches, and the October 2026 edition is not out. max_age_days 400 fails the table if no newer vintage is transcribed within about thirteen months.

Superseded (57): the previous values were declared judgements carried from the earlier implementation with no source and no method, and sat at roughly half of nominal growth (the United States at 2.0% against the 3.59% here). Every DCF-shaped record moves because of it; that is the point of the change, not a side effect.

British Virgin Islands has no row: it is not an IMF member and the World Economic Outlook carries no series for it. A name domiciled there fails naming terminal_growth_rate, as any country absent from this table does. There is no default row; a table with a source has no default.
The class beliefs are offsets around this value, so their centres move with it. No belief was adjusted to offset the change.

Denmark added 2026-09-24 (65) from the same vintage and the same series as every other row: NGDP in Danish kroner at current prices, 3,650,827,415,000 for 2030 and 3,772,961,869,000 for 2031, a change of 3.345%, recorded at 3.35% to the table's precision.

Mexico added 2026-09-29 (71) from the same vintage and the same series as every other row, read from the IMF's own SDMX service (dataflow IMF.RES:WEO, published 2026-04-14, the April 2026 edition) rather than the database's web report, which the same service returned Denmark's two figures from exactly as recorded above, so the vintage is the same one: NGDP in Mexican pesos at current prices, 46,876,709,698,000 for 2030 and 49,446,875,556,000 for 2031, a change of 5.483%, recorded at 5.48% to the table's precision.

unwired._note: Kept verbatim from the original parameter file and not read by the valuation. erp.mode static is the only mode carried forward; rfr_duration is redundant with projection_years, which selects the tenor.

erp._comment_mode: Options: 'static' (Damodaran, from equity_risk_premiums.json) or 'dynamic' (VIX-adjusted). Dynamic mode fetches current VIX and adjusts base ERP: ERP_dynamic = ERP_base × (VIX/VIX_mean)^sensitivity.
erp._comment_vix: VIX historical mean ~19.5. Sensitivity 0.3-0.5 typical. Higher sensitivity = more reactive to VIX changes. Example: VIX=30, mean=20, sens=0.4 → adjustment=1.18 (18% higher ERP).
